newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Milosevic reshuffles party ahead of elections.
newsitem.headline: Milosevic reshuffles party ahead of elections.

text.p: Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic has shuffled the leadership of his ruling Socialist party in a bid to bolster its flagging popularity ahead of presidential and parliamentary elections which must be held this year.

"We have agreed on what to do about the elections and how to win them," Radmilo Bogdanovic, a member of the Socialist Party (SPS) Main Board, said late on Thursday after a meeting of the group. No dates have been set for either vote.
SPS Secretary-General Gorica Gajevic said Thursday's changes in the party leadership were aimed at improving efficiency.
The SPS' popularity plunged in November when it lost control in Serbia's 14 biggest cities, including Belgrade, in local elections.
Milosevic refused to recognise the victories by the opposition Zajedno coalition but three months later he caved in to continuous street demonstrations and intense international pressure.
In February, for the first time since he came to power 10 years ago, Milosevic trailed another politician, Zajedno co-leader Zoran Djindjic, in popularity polls.
According to a poll published in the independent Belgrade newspaper Nasa Borba on Friday, the Zajedno colaition was favoured by 21.6 percent of those questions against 14.9 percent for the SPS.

The Yugoslav news agency Tanjug said Milorad Vucelic, Zivadin Jovanovic and Dusko Matkovic were elected as new deputy chairmen of the SPS. Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic headed the list of the four SPS deputy chairmen.
MIlosevic is the party chairman but he froze the post during his presidency of Serbia.
Vucelic was dismissed from the party leadership after the Dayton peace talks on Bosnia late in 1995 because of his nationalist stance.
Diplomats and opposition leaders believe Vucelic's re-activation shows that Milosevic will once again bank on nationalism as his election campaign ticket.

"The new officials in the SPS are members of the hard-line nationalist faction, which leads me to conclude that SPS will re-embrace nationalist strategy in the election year," Milan Bozic, adviser to Vuk Draskovic, another Zajedno leader, said.

Indeed, the SPS Main Board after Thursday's meeting issued a rallying cry to "all parties, movements, individuals and citizens with sovereignty, dignity and prosperity of the country at hear, to join forces".
The reshuffle also reflects Milosevic's efforts to distance the SPS from the influential but unpopular neo-communist United Left (JUL) led by his wife Mirjana Markovic, diplomats said.
Vucelic and several other new members of the Main Board are disliked by JUL, they said.
